Uniformity and singular scaling follow from explicit eigenvalues. originality.rationale: The 2007 foundational Kaczmarz theorem gives norm-proportional sampling. Gower--Richtarik 2015 gives a general semidefinite optimized-probability formulation rather than these explicit two branches. Agaskar--Wang--Lu 2014 optimizes a different exact asymptotic mean-square error rate. Pukelsheim--Torsney 1991 gives general saturated E-optimality equations but does not state this one-outlier Gram phase transition or the singular unbounded ratio. A published inverse-positive coordinate sampling theorem does not apply: the correlation inverse has strictly negative exceptional-ordinary entries for every r>0. A published cyclic two-row relaxed Kaczmarz result changes algorithm and objective. Mathematical equivalence is considered rather than inferred from title differences; an unknown E-optimal design specialization remains a disclosed risk.
residual_risks: A historical saturated E-optimal-design specialization could contain equivalent closed forms under different notation.

value.rationale: A natural measurement geometry with a single atypical row amid an exchangeable correlated group admits a complete explicit E-optimal law, not merely a special numerical instance. The exact spectral multiplicity transition separates smooth and crossing regimes; uniform selection is optimal iff all pairwise correlations match. A singular weak-coherence family requires exceptional-row sampling on the m^{-1/2} rather than m^{-1} scale and yields arbitrarily large sharp one-step progress improvement over norm-based uniform sampling. These facts guide sampling design and isolate an infinite-family boundary; no claim of downstream wall-clock acceleration is needed.
